child_care_agency: Washington State Department of Children, Youth, and Families (DCYF)
licensing_summary: DCYF licenses child care centers and family homes (up to 12 children) under Chapter 110-300 WAC, and school-age programs under Chapter 110-301 WAC. An agency that regularly provides early learning or child care for less than 24 hours needs a license unless the law excludes it (RCW 43.216.010).
school_age_exemption: Excluded from licensing are seasonal camps, meaning programs that run 3 months or less in any 12-month period and focus mainly on closely supervised recreation or education. Also excluded are programs run by any unit of local, state, or federal government (such as a school district or parks department), schools that accept only school-age children, and drop-in recreation or education programs for school-age children run by a local affiliate of a national nonprofit that follows the national group's safety standards. Programs where parents stay on site are also excluded (RCW 43.216.010(2)). Exempt school-age programs must report their exempt status on a DCYF form (WAC 110-301-0025).
camp_agency: Local health jurisdictions, under State Board of Health camp rules (Chapter 246-376 WAC)
camp_summary: Washington has no youth camp license. Seasonal camps (3 months or less a year, mainly recreational or educational) are excluded from DCYF child care licensing (RCW 43.216.010(2)(g)). Group camps that provide food and lodging must register each year with the local health officer at least 30 days before opening and meet State Board of Health sanitation and site rules (WAC 246-376-010 and -020). Those rules were last updated in 1997.
background_checks_summary: Licensed providers, staff, volunteers, and family-home household members must pass a DCYF background check before having unsupervised access to children, and repeat it at least every 3 years (WAC 110-06-0040; WAC 110-300-0105). The check includes fingerprints, an interstate check for every state lived in during the past 5 years, and disclosure of convictions, pending charges, and 'negative actions' such as founded child abuse or neglect findings. Fingerprints must be redone at renewal only if the person has lived outside Washington since the last check. We found no state background check requirement for seasonal camps, which are excluded from licensing.
medication_summary: Staff may give medication only after completing the program's medication orientation and DCYF's standardized medication administration training. They also need written, signed parent consent and must follow the label. Prescriptions must be for that child and labeled with the child's name, prescriber, dose, and duration. Over-the-counter medication must be in its original packaging, labeled with the child's name, and come with an authorization form. Every dose goes in a medication log (name, drug, dose, date and time, side effects, and the signature of the person giving it), and medication must be stored out of children's reach (WAC 110-300-0215).
mandated_reporting_summary: Mandated reporters include licensed or certified child care providers and their employees, school personnel, DCYF employees, clergy, nurses, and other listed professions. Supervisors at any nonprofit or for-profit organization must also report abuse by someone they supervise who coaches, trains, teaches, or has unsupervised access to children. Reports go to law enforcement or DCYF at the first opportunity, and no later than 48 hours (RCW 26.44.030).
abuse_hotline: 1-866-363-4276 (statewide; DCYF also lists regional intake lines)

child_care_agency: West Virginia Department of Human Services (DoHS), Bureau for Family Assistance, Early Care and Education (child care licensing)
licensing_summary: A child care center license is required for care of 13 or more children in any setting when the facility is open more than 30 days a year per child (78 CSR 1 §2.1; W. Va. Code §49-1-206). Family child care facilities (7 to 12 children) need a certificate and family child care homes (4 to 6 children) need a registration, and centers running out-of-school-time (before/after school, school holiday) programs are licensed under a separate rule, 78 CSR 21.
school_age_exemption: W. Va. Code §49-2-113(e) exempts public-school or WVDE-accredited school programs, school programs with sessions of 4 hours a day or less, summer recreation camps with sessions of 30 days or less, out-of-school-time programs funded and monitored by the WV Department of Education, and out-of-school-time programs for children 6 and older (including programs of national congressionally chartered groups and county parks and recreation or municipal camps) that meet fire and health codes, run state and federal background checks on all staff and volunteers, are not mainly fee-funded (parks and rec and municipal programs excepted) and have a formal monitoring system. Every out-of-school-time program, exempt or not, must register with DoHS when it opens and every year after (§49-2-113(h)).
camp_agency: Local health departments, under the WV Bureau for Public Health, Office of Environmental Health Services (sanitation permit for organized camps)
camp_summary: West Virginia has no youth camp license. Organized camps (places that give children or adults an outdoor group-living experience or have sleeping quarters) need an operating permit from the local health officer under the General Sanitation rule, with plan review for new or remodeled facilities and an inspection before the permit is issued (64 CSR 18 §§64-18-2, 64-18-3). Summer recreation camps with sessions of 30 days or less are exempt from child care licensing (W. Va. Code §49-2-113(e)(3)), and day camps run by county parks and recreation commissions or municipalities can be exempt if they meet the §49-2-113(e)(8) conditions.
background_checks_summary: Licensed centers must have a state and FBI fingerprint-based check run through WV CARES on every staff member and volunteer, and no one may work with children until WV CARES issues a fitness determination; staff stay enrolled in Rap Back for ongoing alerts. Centers must also check sex offender registries and child abuse and neglect registries in West Virginia and in every state lived in during the past 5 years, repeating the abuse registry search every 5 years (78 CSR 1 §8.4). There is no separate camp rule, but out-of-school-time and county parks and recreation or municipal camp programs claiming the §49-2-113(e)(8) exemption must run state and federal checks on all staff and volunteers.
medication_summary: Centers may give medicine only with the parent's written, signed instructions (child's name, medicine, reason, dose, time and route) and, except for limited over-the-counter use, a prescription or written order from a licensed health care provider; prescription medicine must be in its original pharmacy-labeled package, and medicine is kept in a locked container out of children's reach (sunscreen, diaper ointment and emergency medicine need not be locked but must be out of reach). Only staff who have passed approved medication administration training may give it, each dose is recorded in ink in a cumulative medication log, and medication errors must be reported to the director and parent (78 CSR 1 §§8.6.g, 15.4.h).
mandated_reporting_summary: Listed professionals must report, including child care workers, teachers and other school staff, youth camp administrators and counselors, and employees, coaches and volunteers of groups that run organized activities for children. They must report to DoHS immediately and within 24 hours at most, also report to the State Police and local law enforcement when serious physical abuse or sexual abuse is suspected, and tell the person in charge of their program; anyone else may report (W. Va. Code §49-2-803).

child_care_agency: Wisconsin Department of Children and Families (DCF), Division of Early Care and Education, Bureau of Early Care Regulation
licensing_summary: Anyone who cares for 4 or more children under age 7 for pay, for less than 24 hours a day, needs a DCF child care license (Wis. Stat. 48.65(1)). DCF licenses family child care centers (up to 12 children from August 1, 2026), group child care centers (13 or more from August 1, 2026) and day camps, and school-age programs in a licensed center follow the group center rules in DCF 251.
school_age_exemption: The license requirement only covers care of children under 7, so a program serving only children 7 and older does not need a license (Wis. Stat. 48.65(1)). Also exempt: public, parochial and tribal schools, and counties, cities, villages, towns, school districts and libraries running programs mainly for recreation or social purposes (48.65(2)); DCF 251.02 also excludes programs of 4 hours a week or less, group lessons and athletic activities, and seasonal programs of 10 days or less in any 3-month period. School-run programs that want Wisconsin Shares subsidy or YoungStar must be monitored by DCF against part of DCF 251.
camp_agency: Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection (DATCP) and its agent local health departments for overnight recreational and educational camps; DCF for licensed day camps
camp_summary: Overnight camps (recreational and educational camps with overnight living quarters and planned group programs) need an annual license from DATCP or its agent local health department, whether free or fee-based (Wis. Stat. 97.67; ATCP 78.03, 78.07). Day camps caring for 4 or more children under 7 need a DCF day camp license under DCF 252, which covers seasonal, outdoor-oriented programs for children 3 and older. Day camps run by a county, city, village, town, school district or library mainly for recreation are exempt by statute, as are seasonal programs of 10 days or less in any 3-month period (DCF 252.03).
background_checks_summary: Every caregiver, non-caregiver employee and household member (age 10 and up) at a licensed center or DCF-licensed day camp needs a DCF child care background check before starting: Wisconsin criminal history, an FBI fingerprint check, national and Wisconsin sex offender registries, Wisconsin abuse and neglect findings and caregiver misconduct registry, and criminal, sex offender and child abuse registries in any state lived in during the past 5 years. Fingerprints must be redone every 5 years (Wis. Stat. 48.686; DCF 13). DATCP-licensed overnight camps must have applicants disclose sexual criminal history and consent to a check, review the national sex offender public registry before hiring, and adopt a policy barring people with listed offenses (ATCP 78.26(1)).
medication_summary: Staff may give prescription or over-the-counter medicine only with a dated, parent-signed authorization on file listing the child's name and birth date, the medicine, instructions, dosing interval and how long it lasts; blanket authorizations longer than the label allows are not permitted. Medicine must be in its original container labeled with the child's name, dose and directions, stored out of children's reach (refrigerated medicine in a separate labeled container), and given as labeled; new staff orientation must cover medication administration (DCF 251.07(6)(f); DCF 251.05(4)(a)6.).
mandated_reporting_summary: Listed professionals must report, including child care workers in child care centers, child care providers, teachers, school administrators, school counselors and other school employees, social workers, nurses and police (Wis. Stat. 48.981(2)(a)); coaches and recreation staff are not named unless they fit a listed role, though anyone may report. Reporters must tell the county child protective services agency (DCF in Milwaukee County) or the sheriff or local police immediately, by phone or in person (48.981(3)(a)1.); licensed day camp staff and volunteers must also report immediately and get yearly abuse-reporting training (DCF 252.07(3)).
abuse_hotline: No single statewide number: call the county or tribal child protective services agency where the child lives (numbers listed by DCF) or local law enforcement; 911 in an emergency

child_care_agency: Wyoming Department of Family Services (DFS), Child Care Licensing
licensing_summary: Anyone caring for more than two unrelated children must be licensed by DFS unless an exemption applies (W.S. 14-4-102; Ch. 2 §1). License types are family child care homes (up to 10 children in the owner's home), family child care centers (up to 15) and child care centers (16 or more, in a non-residential building) (Ch. 11 §2(a)).
school_age_exemption: Exempt are after-school programs that operate mainly when school is out (before and after school and in summer), serve only children of compulsory school age, are organized for learning, youth development, enrichment, recreation or character-building, and follow local health, safety and fire codes (W.S. 14-4-102(b)(x)). Programs run or supervised by the state, a local government or a school district fall outside the definition of a child caring facility (W.S. 14-4-101(a)(vi)), and summer camps run by nonprofits are exempt (14-4-102(b)(viii)).
camp_summary: Wyoming has no youth camp licensing law in its statutes. Summer camps run by nonprofit organizations are exempt from DFS child care licensing (W.S. 14-4-102(b)(viii)), but a for-profit day camp caring for more than two unrelated children may need a DFS child care license unless another exemption applies, such as the after-school and summer program exemption for children of compulsory school age (14-4-102(b)(x)). 'Ranches for children', including summer-only ranches, are listed as child caring facilities that need DFS certification (W.S. 14-4-101(a)(vi)(J)).
background_checks_summary: Before working, owners, directors, staff, substitutes, volunteers present during operating hours, and household members 18 and older need a Central Registry (child abuse and neglect) check in Wyoming and every state lived in for the past 5 years, national and state sex offender registry checks, an FBI fingerprint check, and state criminal history checks (Ch. 11 §3(g)). The Central Registry and Wyoming sex offender checks repeat every year, and the FBI, state criminal and national sex offender checks repeat every 5 years. No state background check requirement for youth camps was found.
medication_summary: Staff may give medicine only after DFS-approved preservice training that includes medication administration, renewed every 2 years, and with written parent permission for each prescription or over-the-counter medicine (child, medicine, dose, instructions, date and time; for 'as needed' medicine the parent must be called that day first). Prescription medicine must keep its original label, be stored with child-safety caps out of children's reach, and be logged; parents are told the same day, and errors or reactions must be reported to the parent and Licensing within 24 hours (Ch. 11 §17).
mandated_reporting_summary: Every person who knows or has reasonable cause to suspect a child is abused or neglected must report immediately to DFS (the local child protective agency) or local law enforcement (W.S. 14-3-205). Staff of a school, facility or agency must also tell the person in charge, who then also has to make sure a report is made.
abuse_hotline: No single statewide number published: call the local DFS field office (listed on the DFS contact page) or local law enforcement; 911 in an emergency
